theme: O Level English - syllables and sounds
enonce_markdown: How many syllables does the word "banana" have?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

A syllable is a beat with one vowel sound. Say the word slowly and clap at each vowel sound.

### Solution

ba-na-na has three vowel sounds, so three syllables. **Answer: b.**

theme: O Level English - syllables and sounds
enonce_markdown: Which word has the same vowel sound as the underlined letters in "s**ee**n"?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Match words by SOUND, not by spelling. The "ee" in "seen" is the long sound /iː/.

### Solution

"Beach" /biːtʃ/ has /iː/ (spelt "ea"). "Ship" has the short /ɪ/, while "bread" and "bed" have /e/. **Answer: c.**

theme: O Level English - syllables and sounds
enonce_markdown: Which word has the same number of syllables as "education"?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Count the vowel sounds in each word. Split the word into syllables to be sure.

### Solution

e-du-ca-tion has four syllables. Geography (ge-og-ra-phy) has four. Important (im-por-tant) has three, communication (com-mu-ni-ca-tion) has five and university (u-ni-ver-si-ty) has five. **Answer: c.**

theme: O Level English - syllables and sounds
enonce_markdown: Which word has the same consonant sound as the underlined letters in "**ch**urch"?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The same letters can make different sounds. Compare the sound /tʃ/ heard at the start of "church".

### Solution

"Chalk" begins with /tʃ/. "Machine" and "chef" have /ʃ/, and "choir" begins with /k/. **Answer: b.**

theme: O Level English - syllables and sounds
enonce_markdown: Divide each word into syllables with hyphens and state the number of syllables: (i) umbrella (ii) agriculture (iii) hospital.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Divide the word at each vowel sound, then count the parts.

### Solution

(i) um-brel-la: 3 syllables.

(ii) ag-ri-cul-ture: 4 syllables.

(iii) hos-pi-tal: 3 syllables.

theme: O Level English - syllables and sounds
enonce_markdown: Three of these words have the same vowel sound in the underlined letters. Which word is the odd one out? t**ou**gh, en**ou**gh, r**ou**gh, c**ou**gh
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

English spelling is irregular: the letters "ough" are pronounced in different ways. Say each word aloud and compare the vowel sounds.

### Solution

"Tough" /tʌf/, "enough" /ɪˈnʌf/ and "rough" /rʌf/ all have /ʌ/. "Cough" /kɒf/ has /ɒ/. **Answer: d.**
